name: Sarai
overview: Sarai was a female figure in the Bible known primarily as Abram's wife, as explicitly stated in Genesis 11:29. She is a significant Old Testament character whose story is closely tied to the patriarch Abram. There is no record of her tribe or additional notes in the provided information.
namesAndTitles: The name Sarai means 'princess' and is her original proper name given before God renamed her. Later, God gave her the name Sarah, which means 'queen,' reflecting a divine change in her identity and role as recorded in Genesis 17:14.
familyAndRelationships: Sarai was married to Abram, and she is the mother of Isaac, as explicitly noted in Genesis 17:19. She is also described as the lady of Hagar, an inferred relationship from Genesis 16:1. Additionally, she is identified as the daughter of Terah and inferred to be Abram's half-sister according to Genesis 20:12.
scriptureSignificance: Sarai, later known as Sarah, is pivotal in the biblical narrative as the wife of Abram and mother of Isaac, through whom God's covenant promises were fulfilled. Despite her initial barrenness and advanced age, God promised and enabled her to bear a son, demonstrating His faithfulness and power. Her story exemplifies trust in God's promises and is foundational in the lineage of the people of Israel.
